chunks: A man from the companions of Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام complained about his women, so he عليه السلام stood as an orator and said:

O assembly of people, do not obey women in any situation, do not entrust them with wealth, and do not leave them to manage the affair of the dependents. For indeed, if they are left with what they want, they will bring about destruction and transgress the command of the owner. Indeed, we have found that they have no wara' in their need, and no patience in their desire. Extravagance is bound to them even if they grow old, and self-admiration remains attached to them even if they become weak. They do not give thanks for much when they are denied a little; they forget the good and preserve the evil; they rush headlong into calumny, persist in rebellion, and set themselves up for Satan.
So deal with them tactfully in every circumstance, and speak well to them, so that they may act well.

key_terms.الْعِيَالِ: dependents or household members under one's care
key_terms.مَعَاشِرَ: assembly or group being addressed publicly

ai.seo_question: What does this hadith from Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام say about dealing with women in household affairs?
ai.summary: This report describes a complaint brought before Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام, followed by a public exhortation concerning conduct in household and family matters. The passage concludes by instructing people to treat women with tact and kind speech so that good conduct may result.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications:
Hadith.4900 - A man from the companions of Commander of the Faithful (as) complained about his wife.
Commander of the Faithful (as) stood up to deliver a sermon and said:

"O people! Do not obey women in every matter and do not entrust them with wealth. Do not leave them to manage household affairs, for if they are left to act as they wish, they will lead to destruction and overstep the authority of the owner.
Indeed, we have found them lacking in piety when fulfilling their needs and impatient when pursuing their desires. Vanity is inherent in them even as they grow older, and pride clings to them even when they become weak.
They do not appreciate abundance when denied little; they forget the good but remember the bad. They rush into slander, persist in transgression, and align themselves with Satan.
So, handle them with care in all circumstances and speak kindly to them so they may act righteously."
